title: Rabbi Akiva, an Amora
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in the Yerushalmi, Yevamot ch. 2, halakhah 12: "Rabbi Akiva said: Rabbi Chiyya bei Rabbi Shabbetai raises a difficulty," and the Korban HaEdah explains that it is the name of an Amora.
And in Berakhot 55b: "Rabbi Akiva said, Rabbi Panda said," though some read there "Rabbi Ukva."
And in Ketubot ch. 10, halakhah 5: "Rabbi Akiva said before Rabbi Mana."
At the beginning of Jerusalem Talmud Sotah, chapter 3, Rabbi Akiva relates that, after they rose, Rabbi Ba bar Mamal stood with Rabbi Yirmeyah, who raised an objection to him.

notes.text: This entry concerns an Amora named Akiva, with a reported Ukva variant; it does not automatically identify him with the Tanna.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Sotah 3:1 directly names Akiva in the account of Ba bar Mamal and Yirmeyah after the gathering rose. Hyman’s compressed identification of who objected to whom is retained; it does not establish identity with the Tanna. The exact Korban HaEdah explanation and Ukva variant were not independently inspected.
